Below you’ll find several common approaches—command‑line utilities, graphical tools, and even simple scripting—to pull *detailed* information about a specific network interface on most operating systems. Pick the method that matches your environment and what “details” you actually care about (IP config, MTU, driver stats, link state, etc.). --- ## 1️⃣ Command‑Line Methods | Platform | Tool / Cmd | What it shows | |----------|------------|---------------| | **Linux** | `ip -s link show `
or
`cat /sys/class/net//address` | Full NIC statistics + MAC | | | `ethtool ` | Driver/firmware version, speed, duplex, autonegotiation, queue counts | | | `nmcli dev show ` | NetworkManager view – all IPvX configs, DNS, routes | | **macOS** | `networksetup -getinfo Ethernet0` | Interface type, DHCP lease, IP, netmask, router | | | `ifconfig en0` | Low‑level details incl. flags, mtu, tx/rx bytes | | **Windows** | `Get-NetAdapter -Name ""` (PowerShell) | Status, MAC, Speed, LinkSpeed, MediaType | | | `Get-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceAlias ""` | DNS servers per iface | | | `wmic nic where Name="" list full` | OEM vendor data | ### Example: Detailed Linux output (`eth0`) ```bash $ ip -s link show eth0 2: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc pfifo_fast state UP mode DEFAULT group default link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff RX: bytes packets errors dropped overrun mcast 1234567 98765 0 0 0 TX: bytes packets errors dropped carrier collsns 7654321 54321 0 0 0 ``` Add `-j` for machine‑readable JSON: ```bash $ ip -json -s link show eth0 [{"index":2,"if_name":"eth0","flags":["BROADCAST","MULTICAST","UP","DONE","RUNNING"],"mtu":1500,...}] ``` --- ## 2️⃣ Graphical Interfaces | OS | Where to look | Typical fields displayed | |----|--------------|---------------------------| | **Linux (GNOME)** | Settings → Wi‑Fi / Wired → Details | SSID, BSSID, frequency, signal strength, Tx/Rx rates, MAC | | **Ubuntu Server** | `nmtui` → Edit connection → Show advanced options | Same as above plus VLAN tags, bonding settings | | **macOS** | System Preferences → Network → Advanced… | All addresses, routing tables, hardware properties | | **Windows** | Control Panel → Network Connections → Properties → TCP/IP v4/v6 | Addresses, subnet mask, gateway, DNS, adapter index | These GUIs usually expose everything shown by the underlying system calls, so you can cross‑check values against the CLI outputs. --- ## 3️⃣ Programmatic Retrieval If you’re writing a script or monitoring tool, here are quick snippets in popular languages. ### Bash / Shell ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash IFACE="eth0" echo "MAC:" $(cat "/sys/class/net/${IFACE}/address") echo "MTU:" $(cat "/sys/class/net/${IFACE}/mtu") sudo ethtool "$IFACE" | grep -E '(Link detected|speed|duplex)' ``` ### Python (using psutil) ```python import psutil def iface_details(iface): addrs = psutil.net_if_addrs()[iface] stats = psutil.net_io_counters(pernic=True)[iface] print(f"{iface}:") for snicaddr in addrs: print(f" {snicaddr.family.name}:{snicaddr.address}") print("Stats:") print(stats) iface_details('eth0') ``` ### Go (via `golang.org/x/sys/unix`) ```go package main import ( "fmt" "net" ) func main() { ifaces, _ := net.Interfaces() for _, i := range ifaces { fmt.Printf("%v\n", i.Name) } } ``` --- ## 4️⃣ Using SNMP (for remote devices) SNMP provides standardized MIB objects for interface detail: | OID | Description | |-----|-------------| | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.` | IF-MIB::ifDescr | | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5.` | IF-MIB::ifPhysAddress | | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.` | IF-MIB::ifOperStatus | | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10.` | IF-MIB::ifInOctets | | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.16.` | IF-MIB::ifOutOctets | Example using `snmpwalk`: ```bash snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost .1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2 ``` This will enumerate all interfaces and their descriptions. --- ## 5️⃣ Common Pitfalls & Tips | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | You see `` instead of actual name | Run `udevadm trigger --subsystems=usb` or reboot after plugging cable | | No traffic counters appear | Ensure kernel module `nf_conntrack_ipv4` loaded (on some distros) | | Permissions denied when running `ethtool` | Prefix with `sudo` or grant CAP_NET_ADMIN capability | | On Windows, PowerShell cmdlets return empty | Make sure you're running as Administrator or enable Remote Management | --- ## Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Task | One‑liner | |------|-----------| | List all interfaces (names only) | `ip -o link show up | awk '{print $2}'` | | Show IP configuration (IPv4+IPv6) | `hostname -I && ip -6 addr show` | | Check link status | `ethtool eth0 | grep "Link detected"` | | View current route table | `ip r s` | | Dump raw sysfs attributes | `find /sys/class/net/eth0 -maxdepth 1 -printf '%f:%p\n'` | Feel free to adapt any snippet to fit into cron jobs, Ansible playbooks, or custom dashboards. If you have a particular platform or deeper requirement (e.g., fetching QoS marks, checking firmware versions), let me know!
